section_summary.extract_value: This Construct Validity section reports that the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) is positively associated with appearance evaluation (MBSRQ-AE) and general self-esteem (RSES), and negatively associated with Western beauty internalization, dieting, past weight-related teasing, BMI, and multiple eating-disorder symptom scales (EDE-Q subscales, EAT-26). No study label (e.g., 'Study 1') or sample characteristics (sample size, country, demographics, BMI means, survey method) are provided in this text.
section_summary.evidence_source: See Table 3 for correlations between study variables. The BAS was positively correlated with measures of appearance evaluation (MBSRQ-AE) and  general self-esteem (RSES). In contrast, the BAS was  negatively correlated with measures of Western ideal beauty internalization (SATAQ-3 Internalization-General), dieting (EAT-26 Dieting), past experiences of weight-related teasing (PARTS Weight/Size), BMI, and eating disordered symptoms, including dietary restraint (EDE-Q-R), eating concern (EDE-Q-EC), shape concern (EDE-Q-SC), and weight concern (EDE-Q-WC).
